newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker amid see-saw trade.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker amid see-saw trade.

text.p: The Philippine peso slipped to 26.299 to the dollar at the close on Friday, off its day's low of 26.322, and volumes hit a high $229.10 million as traders braced for a five-day weekend.

Dealers said two-way trade was high as banks bought value tomorrow dollars to take advantage of the swap points earned on pesos during the upcoming weekend. Such deals are settled the next trading day.
Banks also sold value today dollars at around 26.28 to remain long on the peso over the New Year holiday.
"Through this scheme, banks will have the pesos they need and earn on the swap points during the weekend," one trader said.
The market will be reopen on Thursday next week.
The dollar-buying hit a plateau at 26.322 when some banks started to unload their dollar holdings.
"Banks are basically long on dollars because of overseas workers' remittances. They decided to take profit when the rate hit 26.322," another trader said.
The Central Bank did not intervene in the market, as it posted its selling rate at 26.33 and buying rate at 26.28.
Traders were expecting the peso to firm up next week due to the steady inflow of dollars.
